findings.title: Weapons queues commands the sim rejects
findings.claim: Space and F queue commands even when a missile is flying; F also queues with an empty magazine or level-2 Weapons damage.
findings.why: Ordinary solo input produces rejected commands, contrary to the client admission requirement.
findings.fix: Check canCharge and canLaunch when building the tick’s commands, accounting for commands already queued that tick; test unavailable states.

findings.title: Tab can invalidate commands queued before the switch
findings.claim: A Weapons command queued in one frame, followed by Tab before the next tick, is sent after that tick’s presence change and rejected as not-at-weapons.
findings.why: This is possible when render frames outnumber sim ticks, and turns an ordinary press into a rejected command.
findings.fix: On Tab, remove or reconcile pending tactical commands from the character being left; add a two-frame, one-tick test.

findings.title: Sampled pointer input survives Tab and restart
findings.claim: The frame samples pointer movement before Tab or Enter clears the pointer, then applies that saved sample to the newly active or reset camera.
findings.why: A drag or wheel event on the switch or restart frame moves a camera that should start from its retained or reset state.
findings.fix: Discard the frame’s sampled pointer delta after Tab or restart, and test both transitions with pending drag and wheel input.

findings.title: Three crowded arrows can overlap after spreading
findings.claim: The spread loop can alternate between two occupied positions and finish on an earlier arrow. For left-edge arrows at y=370, 371, and 372, it produces y=370, 350, and 370.
findings.why: The duel can show overlapping arrows and labels when three targets cluster on one edge; the test covers only two.
findings.fix: Choose an unoccupied edge position monotonically, with edge bounds, and test three and four clustered arrows.

findings.title: Missile prediction starts from a different position than its glyph
findings.claim: The path is predicted from the current sim missile while its visible origin is interpolated from the previous tick.
findings.why: At alpha below 1, the first path segment spans extra movement and the predicted line shifts relative to the drawn missile.
findings.fix: Seed the displayed prediction from the interpolated missile state and add a test with alpha below 1.
